# tech-design conventions

Shared reference for the tech-design skills (start, refine, review, publish). Every skill reads and writes designs by these rules.

<!-- Canonical copy: conventions/CONVENTIONS.md. Copies in skills/*/ are generated by scripts/sync-conventions.sh; edit the canonical copy only. -->

## Layout

One **design** per goal, in its own folder. A repo holds any number of designs.

```
docs/design/<slug>/
  design.md            # the working design: frontmatter + the sections below
  iterations.md        # refinement log, newest entry last
  decisions/NNNN-<title>.md   # one ADR per non-trivial decision
  areas/<area>.md      # deep detail split out of design.md
docs/architecture/
  README.md            # index of published designs
  <slug>.md            # published engineering doc (generated)
  <slug>-summary.md    # published stakeholder one-pager (generated)
```

`<slug>` is kebab-case, short, and names the goal (`link-shortener`, `billing-webhooks`).

## Frontmatter

```yaml
---
title: <human title>
slug: <slug>
kind: greenfield | brownfield
status: draft | refining | ready | published
builds-on: [<other-slug>]   # optional: earlier designs this one extends
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

## Status

| Status | Meaning | Set by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `draft` | v0 written, not yet refined | start |
| `refining` | at least one refinement done | refine |
| `ready` | passes every readiness check | review, when the user accepts |
| `published` | published docs match this design | publish |

Any edit to a `ready` or `published` design sets it back to `refining`.

## design.md sections

Fixed order. Each section stays thin: the whole file aims for 1–2 pages.

1. **Goal**: one paragraph, plus success criteria as a checkable list.
2. **Non-goals and constraints**: what is out, and the tech, budget, team, and existing-system limits.
3. **Current state** _(brownfield only)_: only the parts of the existing system the goal touches, with file paths.
4. **Context**: actors and external systems, C4 level 1 diagram.
5. **Components**: containers/services, one line of responsibility each, C4 level 2 diagram.
6. **Data**: core entities, their owner component, where they are stored, ER diagram.
7. **Key flows**: 1–3 sequence diagrams proving the components deliver the goal.
8. **Migration / delta** _(brownfield only)_: ordered steps from current state to target.
9. **Decisions**: table of `# | Decision | Choice | ADR`.
10. **Open questions and risks**: the refinement backlog (format below).

Cross-cutting topics (access control, deployment, observability, module-level detail) enter only when a refinement settles them, as extra sections between Key flows and Migration / delta, or as area docs.

## Open questions and risks

The single backlog every skill reads from and writes to. One line per item:

```
- [ ] **Q3** (blocking) <question> — _area: data_
- [ ] **R2** (major) <risk> — _area: auth_ — mitigation: <idea or "none yet">
```

- IDs: `Q<n>` for questions, `R<n>` for risks, never reused.
- Severity: `blocking` (design cannot be ready while open), `major`, `minor`.
- Resolved items are ticked and keep a pointer to where they were settled: `- [x] **Q3** ... — settled in ADR 0004`.

## Decisions and ADRs

- Trivial decision (obvious, no real alternative): row in the Decisions table, ADR column `—`.
- Non-trivial decision (real alternatives, or costly to reverse): row plus `decisions/NNNN-<kebab-title>.md`, numbered from `0001`, never renumbered.
- ADR sections, in order: title `# NNNN. <Decision>`, then **Status** (`accepted` | `superseded by NNNN`), **Date**, **Context**, **Decision**, **Alternatives considered** (each with why it lost), **Consequences**.
- A reversed decision gets a new ADR that supersedes the old; the old ADR's status becomes `superseded by NNNN`.

## Areas

When a design.md section passes roughly one page, move its detail to `areas/<area>.md` and leave in design.md a 2–5 line summary plus a link. Area docs follow the same diagram conventions and may hold their own sub-flows.

## iterations.md

One entry per start or refine run, appended:

```
## <n>. <YYYY-MM-DD> — <target area>

- **Changed:** <sections/files touched, one line each>
- **Decided:** <ADR numbers or table rows>
- **New open items:** <IDs, or "none">
```

Entry 0 is the start run (`0. <date> — base design`).

## Readiness checks

A design is **ready** when every check passes:

1. No open `blocking` question or risk.
2. Every success criterion is shown to be met by at least one key flow, or by a cross-cutting section for criteria no flow can show (deployment, operations).
3. Every component appears in at least one key flow or diagram edge.
4. Every entity in Data has exactly one owner component.
5. Every Decisions row has a rationale (inline or in its ADR); every ADR lists rejected alternatives.
6. Every diagram node and edge matches the prose (no orphan names, no undocumented components).
7. Every `major` risk has a mitigation or an explicit acceptance.
8. Brownfield: Migration / delta covers every component that changes.

## Diagrams

Mermaid only, in fenced ```` ```mermaid ```` blocks.

- **Context (L1) and Components (L2)**: `flowchart LR`. The system boundary is a `subgraph`; people as `name([Person])`, external systems as `name[[External]]`, components as `name[Component<br/>tech]`, data stores as `name[(Store)]`. Every edge is labelled with intent and protocol: `-->|"creates link · HTTPS/JSON"|`.
- **Key flows**: `sequenceDiagram`, participants named exactly as the components.
- **Data**: `erDiagram`.
- One diagram per concern; at most ~12 nodes. Split into an area doc beyond that.
